value.first: For 30 months I'd do the 3-day method - three clear days at home, diapers gone on day 1. It's the intensive approach reviewed in the family medicine literature, and it works because diapers hide the feeling of being wet; take them off and a ready child links the urge to the potty fast. Prep this week: pick 3 days at home, put a potty in the room you actually live in, stock salty snacks, drinks she loves and easy-off pants.
value.second: Day 1: let her help bag up the diapers - "your pee and poop go in the potty now." Bare from the waist down all day, push fluids, and the moment pee starts, carry her to the potty mid-stream. Prompt with statements, not questions: "tell me when you need to go." Accidents get one flat, warm line every time - "pee goes in the potty, let's clean it up" - never a sigh or a scold. Nap and night stay in a pull-up you call sleeping pants.
value.third: Day 2: same, plus one 20-40 minute outing commando after a success. Day 3: longer outing, prompt at every transition. Then stay commando for weeks 2-4. Expect "pees with prompting," not done - accidents for weeks, poop lagging pee. If nothing lands by end of day 3, stop cheerfully and retry in 4-6 weeks. Call your doctor if she goes 3+ days without pooping or stools get hard and painful. I'll check in Friday.
